svg.title: The additional first-success wait after three failures has the original geometric distribution
svg.desc: For success probability one quarter and given X greater than three, R equals X minus three is the number of additional trials to first success. Its possible values begin at one. The fresh-wait and conditional additional-wait bars agree at each count one through six, with a final grouped tail for values above six. The exact probabilities are one quarter, three sixteenths, nine sixty-fourths, twenty-seven two hundred fifty-sixths, eighty-one one thousand twenty-fourths, two hundred forty-three four thousand ninety-sixths, and a remaining tail of seven hundred twenty-nine four thousand ninety-sixths. The probability of X greater than five conditional on X greater than three is two hundred forty-three over one thousand twenty-four divided by twenty-seven over sixty-four, giving nine sixteenths, equal to the probability of X greater than two. Conditioning requires positive probability.
